patients.label: 49-year-old woman with post-AF-ablation acute ischemic stroke and incidental MCA aneurysm

identity_evidence.quote: A 49-year-old woman with long-standing atrial fibrillation, maintained on dabigatran 110 mg twice daily, underwent elective catheter ablation.

attribution_limitations: Presenting deficit wording differs: abstract says left hemiparesis and dysarthria; case body says left facial palsy, dysarthria and limb clumsiness (side of limb not stated).
Follow-up duration differs: abstract says asymptomatic at two months; body says three-month follow-up; the anchor (stroke, discharge or aneurysm treatment) is not stated for either.

Occlusion site: text states right M1 occlusion (TOF-MRA and angiography) while the Figure 3A caption states distal ICA/proximal MCA occlusion; the body cites Figure 3A for mTICI 3 recanalization, whereas the caption assigns mTICI 3 and the aneurysm to Figure 3B.
Aneurysm size reported as 7 mm (abstract, discussion) and 7.2 mm (body, Figure 3C caption); title and introduction call it large while the discussion classifies it as moderate-sized and under 10 mm.

Day counters (day 4 dabigatran resumption, day 11 discharge) and One month later (stent-assisted coil embolization) have no explicit anchor; the start of the three-month triple therapy relative to the coil procedure is not stated; "resumed" does not state whether or when dabigatran was held.

Embolic mechanism: cardioembolic source is inferred from gross thrombus appearance and procedural context; microbubble-mediated embolization after radiofrequency ablation is stated as something that "could have contributed". Discussion also says findings suggest a procedural or cardiac source rather than large-artery atherosclerosis.

Order of head CT, idarucizumab and imaging: the text lists head CT, then idarucizumab, rt-PA, MRI/DWI, TOF-MRA and perfusion analysis in narrative order only; times of onset, imaging, rt-PA and EVT are not given. The dabigatran dose-timing before the stroke is not stated.
